prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- A former hospital worker systematically shot and killed four people in upstate New York on Saturday, authorities in two counties said. Former hospital worker Frank Garcia, 34, has been accused in the shooting rampage. Frank Garcia, 34, was arrested Saturday afternoon. Garcia knew all four victims, police said, but they didn't reveal details about the relationships. "The individuals who were shot were known to the suspect. It was not necessarily a random act," Monroe County Sheriff Patrick O'Flynn said. The first two victims -- Mary Sillman, 23, and Randall Norman, 41 -- were fatally shot before 5 a.m. at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, where Garcia was once employed, O'Flynn said. Another woman was wounded and is undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital, he said. The second shooting happened at a house in nearby Ontario County on Saturday afternoon. Christopher Glatz, 45, and his wife, Kim, 38, were killed "execution-style" while their two teenagers were in the suburban Rochester home, Ontario County Sheriff Philip Povero said. The teens were not wounded, but it is unclear whether they witnessed the event. Povero said neighbors reported Garcia went door-to-door looking for the Glatzes' home. "He was in fact looking for the residence," Povero said. "He was saying different things to different people, but he was clearly looking for that home." Ballistic evidence has connected the two crime scenes, Povero said. Investigators found the matching brass cartridges from a pistol found on Garcia when he was arrested, he said. Garcia was arrested at a restaurant Saturday afternoon, CNN affiliate R-News in Rochester reported. Garcia was to be arraigned Saturday night in Monroe County, where the first shootings occurred, on two counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder in the second degree, O'Flynn said. Sillman was a certified nursing assistant at Lakeside's long-term care center, hospital officials said. "During Mary's brief time within the system, those who worked closest with Mary described her as warm, kind and compassionate toward the residents of Lakeside Beikirch Care Center," Lakeside interim CEO Michael Stapleton said in a statement. Garcia likely will face similar charges in Ontario County, Povero said. "This certainly speaks to a tragedy that is enormous, not only the taking of the lives that were taken, but the people that were left behind, the person in Brockport and the two teenage children who were present when their mother was systematically murdered," Povero said.

(CNN) — A former hospital worker systematically shot and killed four people in upstate New York on Saturday, authorities in two counties said.

Frank Garcia, 34, has been accused in the shooting rampage and was arrested Saturday afternoon. Police said Garcia knew all four victims but did not disclose details about their relationships.

“The individuals who were shot were known to the suspect. It was not necessarily a random act,” Monroe County Sheriff Patrick O’Flynn said.

The first two victims—Mary Sillman, 23, and Randall Norman, 41—were fatally shot before 5 a.m. at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, where Garcia was once employed, O’Flynn said. Another woman was wounded and is receiving treatment at a nearby hospital, he added.

The second shooting occurred Saturday afternoon at a home in nearby Ontario County. Christopher Glatz, 45, and his wife, Kim, 38, were killed “execution-style” while their two teenagers were inside the suburban Rochester home, Ontario County Sheriff Philip Povero said. The teenagers were not wounded, although it remains unclear whether they witnessed the killings.

Povero said neighbors reported that Garcia had gone door-to-door searching for the Glatzes’ home.

“He was in fact looking for the residence,” Povero said. “He was saying different things to different people, but he was clearly looking for that home.”

Ballistic evidence connected the two crime scenes, Povero said. Investigators found brass cartridges matching those from a pistol recovered from Garcia when he was arrested, he added.

Garcia was arrested at a restaurant Saturday afternoon, CNN affiliate R-News in Rochester reported. He was scheduled to be arraigned Saturday night in Monroe County, where the first shootings occurred, on two counts of first-degree murder and one count of second-degree attempted murder, O’Flynn said.

Sillman was a certified nursing assistant at Lakeside’s long-term care center, hospital officials said.

“During Mary’s brief time within the system, those who worked closest with Mary described her as warm, kind and compassionate toward the residents of Lakeside Beikirch Care Center,” Lakeside interim CEO Michael Stapleton said in a statement.

Garcia will likely face similar charges in Ontario County, Povero said.

“This certainly speaks to a tragedy that is enormous, not only the taking of the lives that were taken, but the people that were left behind, the person in Brockport and the two teenage children who were present when their mother was systematically murdered,” Povero said.
outputs.L2:
(CNN) — Authorities in two New York counties said a former hospital employee carried out a series of shootings Saturday that left four people dead.

Frank Garcia, 34, was taken into custody Saturday afternoon and accused of committing the attacks. Police said he was acquainted with each victim, although they did not explain the nature of those connections. Monroe County Sheriff Patrick O’Flynn said the shootings did not appear to be random because Garcia knew those who were targeted.

The first attack occurred before 5 a.m. at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, Garcia’s former workplace. Mary Sillman, 23, and Randall Norman, 41, were shot and killed there, according to O’Flynn. A second woman was injured and was being treated at a local hospital.

Later Saturday afternoon, two more people were killed at a residence in neighboring Ontario County. Ontario County Sheriff Philip Povero said Christopher Glatz, 45, and his 38-year-old wife, Kim, were shot in an execution-style manner while their two teenage children were inside the suburban Rochester house. Neither teenager was hurt, though authorities did not know whether they saw the killings.

According to Povero, nearby residents said Garcia had knocked on doors while trying to locate the Glatz residence. Although he gave different explanations to different neighbors, the sheriff said it was evident that Garcia was searching specifically for that house.

Povero said ballistic findings tied the two shooting locations together. Investigators recovered brass cartridge casings that matched a handgun Garcia had with him when he was apprehended.

CNN affiliate R-News in Rochester reported that police arrested Garcia at a restaurant Saturday afternoon. O’Flynn said he was expected to appear in Monroe County court Saturday night on two first-degree murder charges and one charge of second-degree attempted murder stemming from the initial attack.

Hospital officials identified Sillman as a certified nursing assistant at Lakeside’s long-term care facility. In a statement, interim CEO Michael Stapleton said that, despite her short time with the organization, the colleagues who knew her best remembered her as a caring, gentle and compassionate person in her interactions with residents of the Lakeside Beikirch Care Center.

Povero said Garcia would probably face comparable charges in Ontario County. He described the case as an immense tragedy, citing both the four lives lost and the suffering of those who survived—including the injured person in Brockport and the Glatzes’ two teenage children, who were in the house when their mother was deliberately killed.
